title: Regioselective Growth of Mesoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks for the Construction of Anisotropic Nanohybrids
abstract: Abstract Mesoporous anisotropic nanohybrids (m-ANHs) have attracted growing interest because their structural asymmetry enables unique advantages in applications such as multidrug co-delivery and cascade catalysis. However, anisotropic growth in mesoporous systems has thus far been largely confined to an amorphous framework. Achieving regioselective growth of crystalline functional units integrated with mesoporous frameworks remains highly challenging, primarily because of the intrinsic competition at the heterointerface between crystal nucleation/deposition and micelle-directed mesostructural coassembly. Herein, we report an acidity-gated interfacial crystallization-coassembly switching strategy to construct single-crystalline mesoporous MOF (meso-MOF)-based ANHs. This strategy enables the site-selective growth of a new single-crystalline meso-MOF compartment at predefined heterointerfaces, yielding a diverse family of well-defined frame-like, dumbbell-like, and ternary spiny nanohybrids. Mechanistically, precise regulation of the HCl/CH3COOH ratio modulates the nucleation kinetics of MOF precursors, generating localized supersaturation that is sufficient to trigger site-selective heterogeneous nucleation. Concurrently, synchronization of MOF nucleation/growth with interfacial micelle-directed coassembly allows crystallization and mesopore organization to proceed cooperatively. The applicability of this interfacial regulation is demonstrated in several lattice-compatible and chemically stable MOF systems with different compositions and hybrid configurations. As a proof of concept, the hierarchical spiny topology significantly enhances physical bacteria–material interactions, endowing the ternary ANHs with superior antibacterial performance. Remarkably, even in the absence of any drug loading, the ANHs achieve an approximately 90% inhibition efficiency against drug-resistant bacteria. This work establishes a versatile route to regioselectively integrate single-crystalline mesoporous domains into complex anisotropic nanohybrids and highlights the functional potential of structurally programmed crystalline mesoporous interfaces.

title: Hierarchically Porous Polyaniline Film via Interfacial Self-Assembly for Ultrafast Dual-Band Electrochromic Smart Window
abstract: Abstract Dual-band electrochromic smart windows, capable of independently regulating visible and near-infrared solar radiation, offer an effective route toward reducing building/vehicle energy consumption. However, their practical implementation is often limited by slow switching kinetics, insufficient bistability, as well as challenges in fabricating polychromatic, uniform, and scalable electrochromic films with efficient ion and charge transport. Here, we report an interfacial self-assembly strategy to fabricate large-area polyaniline (PANI) thin films featuring a hierarchically porous architecture and thickness-dependent porosity gradient. The self-assembly process, driven by solvent exchange at the air–water interface and modulated by surfactant confinement, produces interconnected PANI nanoparticle networks with both in-plane hierarchical pores and out-of-plane structural gradation. This architecture facilitates electrolyte penetration and charge transport across the film thickness. As a result, the PANI films enable rapid and stable dual-band electrochromic modulation, exhibiting three distinct optical states (“bright”, “cool”, and “dark”) with independent control of visible and near-infrared transmittance. The assembled devices demonstrate fast response (coloration/bleaching times of 1.8/4 s at 633 nm and 1.2/3.6 s at 1200 nm), high coloration efficiency, and excellent optical bistability, together with effective indoor thermal regulation. These results establish interfacial self-assembly as a versatile approach for engineering functional polymer films for next-generation energy-efficient smart windows.

title: Thermally Induced Self‐Assembly of Toroidal Conjugated Small Molecules Enabling High‐Performance Deep Blue Quantum Dot Light‐Emitting Diodes
abstract: ABSTRACT The inferior performance of deep blue quantum dot light‐emitting diodes (QLEDs) compared with red and green counterparts is hindering the commercialization of full‐color QLED display, since their hole mobility of organic hole transport layer (HTL) is lower than the electron mobility of ZnMgO. Although commonly used p‑type small molecules with ordered packing can enhance hole mobility, strong intermolecular interaction causes HTL inhomogeneity and excimer formation. To address this issue, this study designs and synthesizes three propeller‐like molecules, HPB‐6tBu, HPB‐2Cz, and HPB‐6Cz, whose molecular structure suppresses face‐to‐face stacking while allowing for intramolecular toroidal delocalization. Among them, HPB‐6Cz bears superior hole mobility, benefiting from its thermally induced self‐assembly, which simultaneously achieves homogeneous HTL morphology and ordered molecular packing. The intermolecular π–π interaction among HOMO‐located carbazole groups results in a 6.03‐fold enhancement in the hole mobility of HPB‐6Cz upon self‐assembly. Doping HPB‐6Cz into PVK permits ordered packing of PVK and the hole mobility of doped HTL is boosted from 2.21 × 10 −5 to 1.55 × 10 −3 cm 2 V −1 s −1 . Resulting QLED (CIE y = 0.036) based on ZnCdS/ZnS QDs achieves an external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 23.24%, which is the state‐of‐the‐art EQE reported to date. Its operational half‐lifetime also extends from 4321 to 17795 h at 100 cd m −2 .

title: In Situ Polymerization of Covalent Organic Frameworks Networks for Efficient and Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT The crystallization quality and defect density of perovskite films are key factors determining the performance and lifetime of perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Moreover, covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as highly promising multifunctional passivators for PSCs due to their abundant functional groups, periodic pore channels, and excellent chemical stability. However, the strong π–π stacking interactions resulting from the inherently rigid aromatic backbone of COFs lead to extremely poor dispersibility in conventional solvents, severely limiting further improvements in their passivation efficiency and device performance. In response to this issue, we propose a COF‐based synergistic assembly strategy (SAS): introducing two monomers into the perovskite precursor solution and the antisolvent, respectively, to form a COF network via in situ polymerization at grain boundaries during the annealing process. This design not only avoids the agglomeration issues associated with pre‐synthesized COFs, but also effectively regulates crystallization kinetics, passivates defects, suppresses ion migration, and enhances the film's hydrophobicity through the synergistic effects of hydrogen bonding and coordination. The SAS‐treated PSCs achieve a high power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 26.74% and excellent long‐term stability. This strategy provides a new approach to material design for achieving high efficiency and stability in PSCs.

title: Interface-Engineered Flexible Conductive Metal–Organic Framework Films for Multimodal Energy Applications
abstract: Conspectus Conductive metal–organic frameworks (c-MOFs) represent a distinct class of porous conductive materials. Compared with conventional MOFs, c-MOFs integrate intrinsically high electrical conductivity with a high surface area and an ordered porous structure, enabling efficient electron and ion transport. Engineering c-MOFs into continuous and flexible films offers a promising strategy for translating their properties into practical devices. Key strategies for film engineering include solution processing, interfacial growth, and chemical vapor deposition, which allow precise control over the film morphology, thickness, and alignment of conductive channels. Thin-film fabrication preserves structural integrity and pore connectivity, enhances interfacial contact, and facilitates device integration, thereby promoting coupled ionic and electronic transport. These properties render c-MOF films suitable for multimodal energy transformation. In energy storage, their mechanical compliance, flexibility, and high porosity enable conformal integration with deformable and wearable devices while maintaining rapid charge transport and long-term cycling stability. In energy harvesting and conversion, their ordered porous networks, tunable electronic structures, and freestanding mechanically flexible architectures enable efficient adaptation to diverse energy inputs, facilitating energy conversion involving electrical, mechanical, chemical, thermal, and optical processes while maintaining the structural integrity under dynamic deformation. This versatility supports the development of integrated systems capable of simultaneously storing, harvesting, and converting multiple energy modalities for wearable and portable devices. This Account highlights our recent studies on the nanoengineering of c-MOFs on the surface of cellulose nanofibers (CNFs) through interfacial synthesis, enabling the fabrication of freestanding, flexible, and mechanically robust CNF@c-MOF nanopapers, as well as their applications in energy harvesting, conversion, and storage. We discuss the fundamental principles governing the interfacial growth of c-MOF nanostructures on flexible nanofibrous substrates, including the regulation of metal–ligand coordination and interfacial chemical interactions that govern hierarchical assembly toward functional flexible architectures. This Account also summarizes recent advances in the fabrication of flexible c-MOF films, covering representative preparation strategies, structural design approaches, and their unique roles in emerging energy technologies. Future progress in metal center selection, ligand electronic modulation, pore architecture optimization, interface engineering, and composite integration will further improve electron–ion transport, mechanical durability, and device-level compatibility. By combining flexible substrates with multiscale hierarchical structures, flexible c-MOF films can establish interconnected transport networks and adaptive functional interfaces, enabling high-performance, lightweight, and multifunctional energy devices. These advances highlight flexible c-MOF films as a promising platform for next-generation energy technologies that simultaneously demand mechanical flexibility, structural stability, and efficient synergistic electron–ion transport.

title: Emergent Molecular Weaving in an Ionic Metal‐Organic Network for CO 2 Conversion
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular weaving has emerged as a powerful design strategy in supramolecular chemistry, yet most woven frameworks rely on rigid ligands and elaborate templating. Here, we report a minimalistic, aqueous‐phase synthesis of a woven metal‐organic superstructure assembled from Cu 2+ and 2,4,6‐trinitrobenzene‐1,3,5‐triol (TNPG). In the crystal, asymmetric coordination of TNPG with Cu 2+ yields charged one‐dimensional (1D) polymeric strands featuring both distorted octahedral and square planar geometries. These strands interlace at a specific angle to form a two‐dimensional (2D) woven architecture, a rare 1D─1D topological weaving stabilized by hydrogen bonding. The structure also incorporates discrete Cu 2+ cationic complexes, where metal coordination significantly perturbs the aromatic π‐conjugated system of TNPG. These cationic units are tethered within the network through strong hydrogen bonding and electrostatic attraction to the anionic woven strands, contributing to the structural integrity of the superstructure. Given the redox‐active Cu 2+ centers, electronically modulated ligand environment, and framework stability, the Cu‐TNPG network was evaluated for visible‐light‐driven CO 2 reduction. The photocatalytic performance of Cu‐TNPG originates from its high charge separation efficiency and abundant catalytically active sites. Moreover, mild thermal pre‐activation led to enhanced CO evolution efficiency through structural modulations, with a selectivity of ∼85% for CO over H 2 , highlighting its structural and functional versatility.

title: V‐Shaped Linkers Modulate Covalent Organic Frameworks' Interlayer Spacing for Efficient Iodine Capture
abstract: ABSTRACT Significantly enlarging and precisely regulating the interlayer spacing of two‐dimensional covalent organic frameworks (2D COFs) is both meaningful and challenging. Capitalizing on the weak conjugation effects inherent in flexible monomer assembly, this study proposes an interlayer regulation strategy for constructing 2D flexible COFs using dual‐flexible monomers. By introducing nonlinear V‐shaped linkers, we elucidated the core structure‐property relationship of “angle‐packing‐spacing” and established a novel assembly method for synthesizing highly crystalline 2D nonlinear COFs (NLCOFs). Crucially, the V‐shaped topology effectively suppresses interlayer π‐π stacking interactions, thereby enabling controllable expansion and precise tuning of COF interlayer spacing within the range of 4.2 Å to 4.5 Å. Moreover, fine‐tuning the included angle of linkers allows NLCOFs' structural optimization, allowing control over the adsorption and transport properties toward guest molecules such as iodine vapor and iodomethane. This work provides fundamental insights into the rational design of flexible crystalline COFs and establishes a potentially generalizable strategy for interlayer engineering.

title: Continuity-Engineered Single-Atom Chains Regulate Interfacial Microenvironments for Valorized Alcohol Electrooxidation
abstract: Abstract Catalytic selectivity is governed not only by active-site identity but also by the interfacial microenvironments surrounding those sites. Although single-atom chains bridge isolated atoms and extended surfaces, whether their atomic continuity can be exploited as a tunable design parameter for chemical synthesis remains unknown. Here we establish continuity engineering as a strategy for programming catalytic microenvironments through a substrate-anchored synthesis platform that enables precise control over one-dimensional single-atom chain architectures. Using ruthenium chains on α-MnO2 as a model system, we construct catalysts with graded continuity and uncover a volcano-type relationship between chain continuity and synthetic performance during benzyl alcohol electrooxidation. The continuity-optimized catalyst achieves &gt;90% Faradaic efficiency for benzaldehyde across a wide potential window in acidic media while sustaining current densities up to 400 mA cm–2. Mechanistic studies suggest that optimal continuity promotes cooperative water activation, generating a hydroxyl-rich interfacial microenvironment that accelerates alcohol dehydrogenation while suppressing overoxidation. The resulting aldehydes can be directly integrated into one-pot bond-forming (C–S/N coupling) transformations. More broadly, atomic continuity emerges as a design variable for programming catalytic microenvironments and controlling selective electrosynthesis.

title: Chemical Reaction‐Powered Self‐Assembly and Dehydration of Supramolecular Hydrogels for Phase‐Transitional Robots
abstract: ABSTRACT Phase‐transitional robots have long intrigued the scientists from multidisciplinary fields, yet their realization remains a formidable task due to the lack of soft materials that seamlessly integrate phase transition with actuation functionality. Here, we report phase‐transitional hydrogel robots enabled by chemical reaction‐powered supramolecular gelation of a peptide solution followed by a dehydration process. The peptide contains a carboxyl group which can be converted into hydrophobic oxazolone moiety upon addition of carbodiimide. This chemical transformation neutralizes the negative charge of the peptide, thereby activating its self‐assembly into a hydrogel. Interestingly, over time, the hydrogel network becomes more hydrophobic because of the progressive formation of hydrophobic oxazolone species, which in turn leads to dehydration‐induced macroscopic contraction of the hydrogel. The contraction degree can be regulated by changing the concentrations of carbodiimide. This sol‐to‐gel transition followed by actuation behavior enables phase‐transitional robots that can flow into complex terrains to catch and transport cargoes, showing extraordinary morphological adaptivity. As an application, we show that the robot can adaptively enter a narrow channel to regulate an electrical circuit. This work unlocks the potential of chemically fueled supramolecular self‐assembly for the development of phase‐transitional robots that show unparalleled morphological adaptivity and functionalities.

title: Reversible Breathing of Cu─Co Dual‐Atom Sites Enables Spatially Proximal C─N Coupling for Urea Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrocatalytic urea synthesis via the Langmuir–Hinshelwood pathway demands spatially proximal active sites to synchronize the generation and cross‐coupling of C‐ and N‐derived intermediates. Heteronuclear dual‐atom catalysts offer chemically differentiated sites for this purpose, yet whether their bimetallic centers remain static or dynamically evolve during C─N coupling remains unresolved. Here, we construct a well‐defined N 3 ─Cu─Co─N 3 dual‐atom site for the electrochemical coreduction of CO 2 and NO 3 − to synthesize urea and uncover its reversible, electric‐field‐driven structural breathing under electrocatalytic conditions, affording a maximum urea yield rate of 4828.4 ± 136.5 µg h −1 mg cat −1 and a Faradaic efficiency of 56.8 ± 7.6% at −1.2 V (vs. RHE). Operando x‐ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) revealed a reversible, electric‐field‐driven breathing‐like modulation of the Cu─Co distance, characterized by Cu─Co contraction and Cu─N/Co─N elongation. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations show that the Cu─Co distance reaches a minimum of 2.16 Å in the *CONH 2 ‐bound configuration formed during the initial C─N coupling step. The adaptive contraction brings C‐ and N‐intermediates into close proximity to enable C─N coupling, thereby reconfiguring heteronuclear dual‐atom sites from static pairs into dynamically responsive centers and highlighting field‐tunable metal–metal distance as a catalytic design lever.

title: Enzymatic In Situ Self‐Assembly of a Fluorogenic Photosensitizer Induces PANoptosis for Photodynamic‐Immunotherapy
abstract: ABSTRACT PANoptosis, an inflammatory programmed cell death that integrates pyroptosis, apoptosis, and necroptosis, holds great promise for cancer immunotherapy. However, conventional strategies relying on PANoptosome assembly are hindered by complex upstream signaling requirements. Here, we report P–CHD–TPP, an enzyme‐instructed in situ self‐assembling probe that triggers PANoptosome‐independent PANoptosis via persistent mitochondrial disruption. Upon alkaline phosphatase (ALP)‐triggered dephosphorylation, P–CHD–TPP self‐assembles into fluorescent nanoparticles decorated with triphenylphosphonium (TPP) and 1,3‐cyclohexanedione (CHD) groups, which are rapidly internalized by tumor cells and preferentially accumulate in mitochondria. The TPP groups in the assembled nanoparticles moderately disrupt mitochondrial homeostasis, leading to protein sulfenylation. Then, the CHD moiety covalently labels and inactivates these sulfenylated proteins, effectively disabling the endogenous reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging system. Upon near‐infrared irradiation, a massive ROS burst is generated, inflicting severe and sustained mitochondrial damage. This cascade induces rapid PANoptosis‐associated pathways and triggers profound mitochondrial DNA release to activate the cGAS–STING pathway. The combined activation elicits robust antitumor immunity, effectively suppressing orthotopic 4T1 tumor growth and prolonging survival. This work establishes a mitochondrial sulfenylated protein‐labeling strategy that amplifies oxidative stress, providing a paradigm for PANoptosis‐based photodynamic‐immunotherapy.

title: Aligned Self-Assembled Nanostructure by Chemical Force Trigger, Biased Migration, and Oscillatory Hydrogel Growth
abstract: Abstract Cells generate pico-to-nanonewton forces through metabolic circuits and diffusion for downstream processes, including stress fiber assembly and cellular growth. The inherent complexities of the system’s processing, reactivity, and adaptability make it difficult to recapitulate in a synthetic setting. Herein, we compartmentalized the urease-urea feedback-controlled reaction network (FCRN), demonstrating global vs local function adaptability by coupling with peptide self-assembly. Compartmentalized FCRN (c-FCRN) facilitates chemical energy-to-mechanical energy conversion, creating forces on the piconewton scale, allowing nanofiber alignment, akin to what a cell does. The trade-off between multiple microscale interactions in the chemo-material network implies molecular-biased migration resembling chemotactic-like directed motion in synthetic settings, which promotes spatial self-assembly remodelling. Consequently, regulating the reaction-diffusion chemistry, we demonstrate oscillatory hydrogel growth by encasing the c-FCRN with a physical membrane barrier. Furthermore, c-FCRN provides a rudimentary structure-building system to create various complex hydrogel structures, bypassing the 3D printing tools. Thus, the chemo-material network provides proof-of-concept for biomimetic material development by emulating biologically inspired technologies.

title: Micelles as a Confined Liquid: Standard and Two-Dimensional Kinetics of Solute Rotation in Surfactant Micelles
abstract: Abstract The dynamics inside a surfactant micelle show clear confinement effects: solute rotation slows and develops a nonexponential relaxation. Multiple rate constants─rate dispersion─must be involved. These effects have been widely attributed to solutes confined to an outer layer of strongly ordered hydrocarbon chains, a layer similar to a Langmuir-Blodgett film. In this picture, confinement effects result from a surface phenomenon enhanced by the high surface area of a nanometer-sized particle. This paper presents results that are inconsistent with strong chain ordering. Varying the solute shows that most of the confinement-induced slowing is at the center of the micelle, not near its surface. Two-dimensional (two-relaxation-period) kinetics show that rate dispersion is mostly due to rate heterogeneity among different solute molecules. A homogeneous component of the stretched dynamics is also identified and is attributed to the coupling of the solute rotation with conformational relaxation of the hydrocarbon chains. In a picture consistent with these results, the micelle is unstructured, and the solutes are more widely distributed than in the conventional model. Confinement effects are not due to surface effects; they are due to the clash in the lengths of the hydrocarbon chain and the particle diameter. This study is enabled by a nonparametric, “data-first” approach that enhances the interpretation of kinetics, especially two-dimensional kinetics.

title: A Photosensitizer Bearing an Asymmetric “Push-Pull” Bipyridine Ligand Enhances Excited State Electron Transfer
abstract: Abstract Herein we report RuII photosensitizers that bear a single “push-pull” ligand designed to polarize charge on a single pyridine ring of 2,2′-bipyridine (bpy) in the metal-to-ligand charge-transfer (MLCT) excited state for enhanced excited state electron transfer. The photosensitizers have the general structure [Ru(dtb)2(4-CO2H,4′-R-bpy)]2+, where R is –H (RuHcb), −CF3 (RuFcb), and −CH3 (RuMcb) and dtb is 4,4′-(tert-butyl)2-bpy. These photosensitizers were synthesized, characterized spectroscopically and electrochemically, and contrasted with [Ru(dtb)2(dcb)]2+ (RuDcb) that bears the more common dicarboxylic acid ligand, Dcb = 4,4′-(CO2H)2-bipyridine. When anchored to mesoporous TiO2 thin films in a 0.1 M LiClO4/CH3CN electrolyte, RuMcb|TiO2 displayed the largest excited state electron injection yield ϕinj = 0.90 and, generally, ϕinj decreased as R became more electron withdrawing. RuDcb|TiO2 displayed a significantly lower ϕinj = 0.80. Transient absorption spectra recorded on ps and ns time scales and spectroelectrochemical data revealed that ∼70% of the total ϕinj for RuMcb occurred on a sub ps time scale that could not be kinetically resolved, only 20% occurred on this same time scale for RuDcb. Quantum chemical simulations were utilized to characterize the charge transfer excited states, the surface binding, and the interfacial electron transfer kinetics. Apart from RuFcb, the data reveal that the push–pull ligand had little impact on the ground state and a significant one on the MLCT excited state, polarizing charge on a sub-ps time scale for more efficient interfacial electron transfer. More broadly, the data reveals that push–pull ligands can be optimized for excited state electron transfer reactivity.

title: Metal-organic framework/MXene composites: design strategies and applications for energy storage, catalysis, and sensing
abstract: Metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), as crystalline porous materials with tunable chemical compositions, have attracted widespread interest for energy-related applications. However, their low electrical conductivity and limited structural stability under electrochemical conditions restrict practical deployment. Integrating MOFs with two-dimensional transition metal carbides/nitrides (MXenes) creates composite materials that combine the high surface area and active sites of MOFs with the metallic conductivity and mechanical flexibility of MXenes. This review summarizes recent progress on MOF/MXene composites. The major synthetic routes are classified into four categories: in situ growth with interfacial chemical bonding, electrostatic self-assembly, post-synthetic transformation into metal oxides, sulfides, and phosphides, and interface engineering. Their applications are discussed across electrochemical energy storage (lithium, sodium, potassium, and zinc-ion batteries, and supercapacitors), energy conversion (electrocatalytic hydrogen/oxygen evolution, oxygen reduction, and photocatalysis), and sensing. Despite research advances, challenges remain for practical application, including MXene oxidation during processing and operation, difficulties in large-scale fabrication with batch-to-batch consistency, and the need for precise interfacial regulation. Finally, future research directions are outlined, including artificial intelligence-assisted material screening, construction of three-dimensional hierarchical structures, and evaluation of industrial applicability through standardized testing protocols.

title: Metal–Organic Framework Synthesis Strategies for Efficient Encapsulation and Sustained Release of Bioactive Compounds
abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as versatile carriers for biomedical applications because of their tunable porosity, high surface area, and structural robustness. Their biocompatibility depends on carefully selecting nontoxic metals such as Fe, Zn, or Mg; safe organic ligands, including carboxylates, imidazolates, and pyridines; and stabilizing coatings such as polyethylene glycol (PEG), chitosan, and polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) that enhance aqueous stability and enable controlled release. Conventional synthesis methods typically yield highly crystalline frameworks but require long reaction times and extensive solvent use. In contrast, nonconventional approaches are gaining popularity for their faster, energy‐efficient methods. Techniques such as microwave irradiation, sonochemical activation, and electrochemical synthesis provide rapid, controllable conditions that reduce energy consumption and shorten reaction times. In particular, mechanochemical encapsulation is an eco‐friendly, sustainable, scalable, and high‐yield methodology that enables in situ entrapment of bioactive molecules and enhances adsorption capacity. Moreover, the mechanochemical methodology enables modulation of physicochemical parameters such as morphology and particle size, which critically influence adsorption behavior and host–guest interactions. Examples of encapsulation processes involving antidiabetic agents, anticancer therapeutics, and antioxidants are presented, and these can be translated into mechanochemical approaches. In this regard, MOFs stand out as promising platforms for targeted delivery and sustained release. Integrating rational component selection, coating strategies, and sustainable synthesis methodologies positions MOFs as next‐generation biocompatible carriers for precision biomedical applications.

title: Framework Bond Chemistry Governs Seed Activity through Molecular Precursor Regulation in SSZ-39 Crystallization
abstract: Abstract Seed-assisted synthesis is widely used to accelerate zeolite crystallization, yet the molecular origin of differences in seed activity remains unclear. Here, we show that seed activity in SSZ-39 crystallization is governed by framework bond chemistry and its control over the dissolved molecular precursor ensemble. By combining Fourier-transform ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS), magic-angle-spinning solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance (MAS ssNMR) spectroscopy, crystallization kinetics, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations, we compare SAPO-18, NH4A, homologous SSZ-39, and seed-free systems. All systems yield phase-pure AEI zeolite, but their crystallization rates differ sharply: SAPO-18 completes crystallization within 12 h, approximately six times faster than the seed-free system. FT-ICR MS reveals that active seeds shift aluminosilicate precursors toward low-condensation oligomers (&lt;6 T atoms) and enrich the corresponding OSDA-associated complexes. DFT calculations show that these low-condensation aluminosilicates interact more strongly with DMDMP cations than more highly condensed counterparts, linking precursor speciation to OSDA utilization and nucleation. The exceptional activity of SAPO-18 arises from facile alkaline hydrolysis of weak P–O–Al linkages, which promotes extensive seed dissolution, while the released phosphate remains outside the SSZ-39 framework. In contrast, stronger Si–O–Al and Si–O–Si linkages in aluminosilicate seeds limit dissolution and generate less favorable precursor ensembles. These results identify framework bond chemistry as a molecular descriptor of seed activity and recast zeolite seeds as chemical regulators rather than passive structural templates, providing a basis for rational and lower-OSDA zeolite synthesis.

title: A single-molecule spin–photon interface
abstract: Abstract Optical interfaces that connect long-lived spin qubits to photons are a central requirement for quantum networking and distributed quantum information processing. At present, solid-state atomic defects are leading candidates because of their inherent spin and optical coherence 1,2 . Building on these advancements, synthetically tailored molecular systems represent a fundamental change in the field, using precise atomic control and consistent bottom-up assembly 3,4 . However, a molecular platform that concurrently satisfies the demands of a robust spin–photon interface—namely, the combination of bright fluorescence, high spectral stability and long ground-state spin lifetimes—has yet to be realized at the single-molecule level. Here we show that a triplet ground-state carbene molecule, embedded within a structurally matched host crystal, functions as a robust spin–photon interface with single-molecule addressability. The system exhibits narrow ZPLs, spectral stability over more than an hour, spin-selective optical transitions and single-molecule optically detected magnetic resonance. Coherent control yields millisecond-scale dynamical-decoupling coherence and tens-of-milliseconds spin relaxation at a temperature of 4.5 K. These results establish molecular qubits as a viable platform for single-emitter quantum optics 5,6 while preserving the advantages of bottom-up chemical design 7 and processable materials 8–10 .

title: Atomic‐Shell Amplification of Intrinsic Coordination Asymmetry Enables Giant Optical Nonlinearity
abstract: ABSTRACT Developing bulk nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals that simultaneously combine outstanding optical performance with excellent crystal growth capability remains a major challenge. Here, we introduce an intrinsic coordination asymmetry strategy that exploits highly polarizable tetrahedral Hg–S coordination and conformationally flexible ligands to amplify local structural distortions within discrete homoanionic modules. Guided by this concept, Cc ‐(NH 4 ) 2 Hg(SCN) 4 ( Cc ‐AHT) and its C 2/ c polymorph were synthesized. Structural and theoretical investigations reveal that the flexible (SCN) − ligands propagate distortions originating in the [HgS 4 ] core throughout the [Hg(SCN) 4 ] 2− module, establishing an atomic‐shell distortion amplification model that quantitatively traces the evolution of local coordination asymmetry. Cc ‐AHT exhibits a giant second‐harmonic generation response (14 × KH 2 PO 4 and 1.2 × KTiOPO 4 at 1064 nm), a band gap of 3.25 eV, and large birefringence (Δ n = 0.341 at 1064 nm), while centimeter‐sized single crystals can be readily grown under mild conditions. This work establishes intrinsic coordination asymmetry and its atomic‐shell amplification as a chemically guided strategy for designing high‐performance homoanionic NLO materials and provides a general framework for understanding how local structural distortions propagate through coordination modules containing conformationally flexible ligands.

title: Processing Window Expansion Enables Uniform Crystallization in Scalable Ambient‐Fabricated Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT Slot‐die coating is a promising scalable deposition technique for perovskite devices due to its high material utilization and inherent compatibility with continuous manufacturing. However, a narrow deposition‐to‐annealing time window and inhomogeneous ink distribution limit the device performance. Herein, we report a combined additive (CA) strategy that simultaneously regulates nucleation kinetics and phase evolution, broadening the processing window for slot‐die coating in the ambient. By synergistically introducing rubidium thiocyanate (RbSCN) and formamidinium thiocyanate (FASCN), an in situ coordination mechanism is established that lowers the energy barrier for the δ‐to‐α phase transition while suppressing non‐photoactive phase formation. This leads to uniform crystallization over an extended time window exceeding 100 s, yielding dense large‐grained α‐FAPbI 3 films with minimized vertical compositional gradient and reduced residual strain. The resulting films exhibit suppressed defects, prolonged carrier lifetime, and optimized energy‐level alignment, enabling efficient charge extraction and reduced nonradiative recombination. The CA strategy enables highly uniform large‐area deposition to deliver an efficiency of 22.70% for perovskite solar modules. Meanwhile, the unencapsulated devices maintain 97.76% of the initial efficiency under ISOS‐L‐3 for 1300 h. This CA strategy establishes a generalizable pathway for decoupling crystallization kinetics from processing constraints, providing a robust method for scalable high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Threo‐Chiral Cation Additive Enables Ordered Lattice Adsorption and Enhanced Operational Stability of Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT Chiral molecular engineering is an effective strategy to modulate crystallization and mitigate nonradiative defects in perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, unconstrained bond rotation often leads to spatial mismatch between chiral molecules and the perovskite lattice, hindering effective defect coordination. Herein, we introduce threo‐chiral cation additive of (2 S ,3 R )‐2‐amino‐3‐hydroxybutanamide hydrochloride (ThrA) to achieve precise perovskite lattice regulation. Benefiting from methyl‑induced steric hindrance originating from its dual chiral‑center threo‑configuration, ThrA acquires a conformationally locked rigid stereostructure and further facilitates thermodynamically‑favored parallel‑to‑lattice multi‑site synergistic adsorption via hydrogen bonding and Pb coordination. Such stereoselective “lock‐and‐key” interaction reduces lattice surface energy, guides preferential (100) crystal growth, and simultaneously suppresses lattice distortion and ion migration. Consequently, the ThrA‐modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion efficiency of 26.68% (certified 26.31%), while 65 cm 2 large‐area module delivers a promising PCE of 22.78% (certified 22.12%), representing one of the outstanding certification efficiencies for perovskite modules of comparable size. Unencapsulated devices retain 90% of their initial efficiency after 1000 h thermal aging (ISOS‐D‐2) and maintain 92% performance after 2000 h continuous maximum power point tracking (ISOS‐L‐2). This work demonstrates that the stereostructure of additive is decisive for precise perovskite crystallization modulation, providing advanced stereochemical strategy toward high‐efficiency and ultra‐stable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: A Precursor Design Principle for Archipelagic Hard‐Carbon Structural Evolution Through Cohesion–Solvation Regulation of Asphaltene Molecular Heterogeneity
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium‐ion batteries are central to the development of affordable electrochemical storage for renewable energy integration. Yet hard‐carbon anode design lacks a precursor‐level principle linking molecular assembly in chemically heterogeneous feedstocks to oxidative stabilization and closed‐pore formation. Here we establish a precursor‐level cohesion‐solvation design principle for regulating molecular selection and assembly in heterogeneous aromatic feedstocks. Toluene‐fractionated asphaltene precursors undergo oxidative crosslinking, redirecting carbonization from continuous coke‐like growth toward separated turbostratic domains and confined closed pores. A hard‐carbon performance screening index (HPSI) quantifies structural and electrochemical performance, while density functional theory (DFT) reveals stronger Na affinity and lower migration barriers in defect‐engineered carbon galleries. The solvent‐selected AHC‐80‐1400 delivers 400.1 mAh g −1 at 0.05 A g −1 with 87.7% ICE and retains 92.3% capacity after 10 000 cycles, while sustaining wide‐temperature sodium storage with 91.8% and 90.4% retention at −20°C and 50°C, respectively. At scale, a 10‐kg batch enables a 1.18 Ah NFM||AHC‐80‐1400 pouch cell, delivering 163.3 Wh kg −1 and 95.5% retention after 700 cycles. A cradle‐to‐gate life‐cycle assessment (LCA) shows that AHC‐80‐1400 production reduces climate‐change impact by 33.7% relative to Commercial HC. These findings establish precursor‐stage molecular selection as a design principle for harnessing feedstock heterogeneity to control carbonization trajectories and electrochemical function.

title: pH-Responsive Supramolecular Self-Assembly of an Aromatic Zwitterionic Surfactant-Polyamine System for High-Temperature Clean Fracturing Fluids
abstract: Abstract To address the thermal limitations inherent to conventional viscoelastic surfactant (VES) fracturing fluids, a novel aromatic zwitterionic surfactant, erucamidopropyl dimethyl carboxybenzyl ammonium chloride (ECBA), was synthesized and formulated with diethylenetriamine (DETA) to construct a supramolecular clean fracturing fluid (CFF) system. Comprehensive rheological evaluations revealed that the ECBA/DETA system achieved optimal performance at a total concentration of 4.0 wt % and pH 3.95. Mechanistically, the pH-responsive protonation of the carboxyl and amino moieties synergistically reinforced intermolecular electrostatic interactions and hydrogen bonding, driving the self-assembly of a robust supramolecular network. Cryo-SEM observation, combined with DLS measurements and packing parameter analysis, revealed a distinct porous network morphology and provided complementary evidence for the pH-dependent self-assembly and viscoelasticity of the system. Consequently, the optimized fluid exhibited elastic-dominated viscoelastic behavior with outstanding thermal and shear stability up to 110 °C. At 90 °C, the proppant settling velocity was remarkably suppressed to 0.750 cm/min, indicating superior proppant-carrying capacity. Furthermore, the incorporation of a DTPA chelating agent significantly enhanced the system’s resistance to Ca2+ ions. Regarding reservoir protection, complete gel breaking was achieved within 1 h using 10% kerosene at 90 °C, yielding an ultralow residue content of 0.147 mg/L. The resulting gel breaking fluid displayed reduced surface and interfacial tensions (22.7 and 0.051 mN/m, respectively), a high clay antiswelling efficiency of 85%, and favorable emulsification/demulsification behavior. Collectively, these results demonstrate that the synergistic noncovalent interactions between the aromatic zwitterionic surfactant and DETA under acidic conditions effectively stabilize the supramolecular network, providing a promising molecular design strategy for high-temperature and formation-friendly CFFs.

title: Nonfullerene Acceptor−Iridium Coordination Polymer as a Triplet Sensitizer for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT Utilizing triplet excitons has been recognized as a promising method to boost performances of organic solar cells (OSCs). Although long lifetime and diffusion length of triplet excitons have been observed in some systems, efficiencies of triplet‐sensitized OSCs are still moderate because of the lack of an efficient way to generate and transfer triplet excitons. In this study, we report a nonfullerene acceptor–iridium coordination polymer (BTP‐N‐Ir) as a triplet sensitizer in ternary OSCs for utilizing triplet excitons to improve photocurrents. The triplet polymer sensitizer shows a small singlet‐triplet energy gap, facilitating the generation of long‐lived triplet excitons, which transfer to an intra‐moiety excited (i‐EX) state of the acceptor in ternary films, dissociating into free charges to contribute photocurrents. Such a new triplet‐exciton transfer pathway with the i‐EX as an intermediate state is more effective than those in previous systems, leading to the highest efficiency of 20.37% for OSCs with a triplet sensitizer.

title: 3D Cuprous Iodide Cluster‐Covalent Organic Framework for Ultrasensitive and Highly Selective Trace HF Detection at Room Temperature
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrofluoric acid (HF) poses a serious and irreversible threat to human health necessitating the development of highly sensitive and selective detection materials. Herein, a three‐dimensional cuprous iodide cluster‐based covalent organic framework (CuI‐MCOF), with diamond topology has been successfully prepared, which shows an ultrafast and highly sensitive response to HF gas. At room temperature, CuI‐MCOF displays an exceptional response of 7188% toward 100 ppm HF, with remarkably rapid response/recovery times of 3 s/2 s at 4 ppm. Notably, the sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of 21 ppb, outperforming previously reported HF sensors. Moreover, it demonstrates outstanding selectivity and anti‐interference performance, maintaining stable responses to 4 ppm HF even in the presence of 16 interfering gases (100 ppm each). Experiments combined with density‐functional theory calculations reveal that the imine‐linker N atoms serve as reversible HF adsorption–desorption sites, while the electron‐rich CuI clusters enhance dipole interactions and facilitate charge transfer. Leveraging these properties, an on‐chip miniaturized perceptron system integrated with evaluation algorithms is developed for anti‐interference HF discrimination, spatiotemporal distribution estimation, and leakage source prediction. This work provides a new strategy for designing high‐performance HF sensors and expands the application of cluster‐based COFs in gas sensing.

title: Beyond Linker Length: Three-Dimensional Linker Geometry Governs Flexibility in Zn–Triazolate MOFs
abstract: Abstract Flexible metal–organic frameworks undergo cooperative structural transformations that underpin applications in molecular separations, sensing, and gas storage; however, the molecular origins of framework flexibility remain poorly understood. Here, we investigate the role of linker geometry in directing the structural response of a family of isoreticular Zn–triazolate pillared-layer MOFs incorporating cubane (cdc), bicyclo[1.1.1]pentane (pdc), and bicyclo[2.2.2]octane (boct) dicarboxylate linkers. Variable-temperature and in situ CO2 powder X-ray diffraction, variable-temperature single-crystal X-ray diffraction, gas adsorption measurements, and machine-learning-enabled atomistic simulations reveal fundamentally different mechanical responses despite the frameworks possessing closely related architectures. The cdc framework exhibits reversible cooperative breathing, the pdc analogue undergoes pathway-dependent structural reorganization consistent with kinetic trapping following cooling of the activated framework to 77 K, whereas the boct framework accommodates deformation through continuous elastic distortion without discrete phase transitions. Computational analysis demonstrates that these contrasting behaviors arise primarily from the manner in which linker geometry governs strain accommodation within the flexible Zn–triazolate sheets, rather than from the deformation of the linker itself. These results establish structure–mechanics relationships across this family of flexible MOFs and demonstrate that subtle changes in molecular geometry provide a powerful strategy for programming cooperative structural behavior.

title: Harnessing the Hard‐Soft Acid‐Base Principle in Sulfur‐Dense Flexible Covalent Organic Frameworks for Targeted Gold Sequestration
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient gold (Au) recovery from e‐waste and industrial effluents is crucial for sustainable resource management, yet building crystalline covalent organic frameworks (COFs) with dense sulfur soft sites under Hard‐Soft Acid‐Base (HSAB) guidance is severely hindered by the intrinsic rotational freedom of thioether linkages, which typically precipitates amorphous networks. Herein, we report the rational synthesis of sulfur‐bridged flexible COFs by tailoring solvothermal kinetics to enable the construction of crystalline topological framework isomers ( sql and kgm nets) from an identical tetracyclic C‐S bond‐enriched monomer. The kgm framework was further functionalized with pendant methyl sulfide groups, generating abundant soft binding sites. Consequently, the resulting electron‐rich framework delivers an exceptional Au uptake capacity of 6420 mg g −1 , ranking among the highest values reported to date for COFs under dark conditions, alongside rapid uptake kinetics and excellent selectivity. Combined spectroscopic and theoretical investigations reveal that sulfur sites play a central role in Au capture by providing abundant active sites, facilitating the coordination of Au species, and promoting electron transfer, thereby favoring the reduction of Au(III) to Au(0). This paradigm underscores the potency of the HSAB principle as a robust blueprint for designing high‐performance adsorbents aimed at the sustainable precious metal recovery.

title: Coupling Ligand Tuning With Polymer‐Induced Aperture Regulation for Molecular Sieving in Flexible MOFs
abstract: ABSTRACT Framework flexibility fundamentally limits molecular sieving in many metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) by enlarging their effective pore apertures beyond crystallographic constraints. This challenge is pronounced in zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8 (ZIF‐8), where dynamic aperture expansion prevents CO 2 /N 2 size‐sieving despite an ideally positioned nominal aperture size. Here, we show that polymer infiltration enables in situ regulation of dynamic apertures, converting ZIF‐8 from a nonselective adsorbent into a CO 2 /N 2 molecular sieve. During mixed‐matrix membrane (MMM) formation, poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) partially infiltrates ZIF cavities and suppresses framework dynamics, as supported by solid‐state NMR ( 1 H‐ 13 C HetCor) and spin–lattice relaxation. Consequently, the CO 2 /N 2 diffusion selectivity of ZIF‐8‐NH 2 with 6 mol% 2‐aminobenzimidazole increased from 0.58 (polymer‐free) to 26.6 within the polymer environment, enabling CO 2 /N 2 size sieving. Membranes with 20 wt% filler achieved a CO 2 permeability of 261.7 Barrer and a CO 2 /N 2 selectivity of 73.9. This strategy is generalizable to other flexible ZIFs, such as ZIF‐7 and ZIF‐67, establishing polymer infiltration as a simple and versatile route for controlling dynamic MOF apertures for effective gas separation.

title: HOMO‐Level Alignment as a Design Descriptor for Donor–Acceptor Covalent Organic Frameworks in Aqueous Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc–iodine batteries (ZIBs) offer high voltage and inherent safety, but face a persistent trade‐off among fast kinetics, long cycling stability, and high iodine loading. Donor–acceptor (D–A) covalent organic frameworks (COFs) have emerged as promising iodine hosts, yet the rational design is hindered by an unclear understanding of what truly governs charge‐transfer efficiency—with most studies empirically pursuing higher energy density without clear design rules. In this study, we establish highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) level alignment relative to iodine's redox potential as the governing descriptor for charge‐transfer efficiency. Analyzing a series of units with progressively elevated HOMO levels reveals a clear trend: higher HOMO levels enhance electron donation to iodine and promote charge transfer. The optimally designed NT‐COF, which combines a triphenylamine (TPA) donor with favorable HOMO alignment and a naphthalene diimide (NTCDI) acceptor with extended conjugation, exhibits the best electrochemical performance. Even with a high iodine loading (∼50.5 wt%), it delivers stable cycling and reliable low‐temperature operation. Spectroscopic and theoretical analyses confirm that the energetic alignment facilitates chemisorptive iodine anchoring, accelerates charge transfer, and suppresses polyiodide dissolution. This synergy confirms that rational COF design must combine energy‐level alignment with structural conjugation.

title: General Synthesis of Inverse Opal Covalent Organic Framework Photonic Crystals
abstract: Abstract Constructing highly crystalline inverse opal covalent organic framework photonic crystals (IO COF PhCs) remains challenging due to the incompatibility between the spatial confinement required for inverse opal replication and the synthesis process of COFs. Inspired by the semi-solid chitin infiltration and confined solidification process in beetle photonic architectures, a solvent-free template-assisted melt pressing (STAMP) strategy is developed for the general synthesis of crystalline IO COF PhCs. The quasi-solid precursor state facilitates efficient template infiltration while remaining reactive for COF crystallization, affording ordered macroporous photonic architectures within 3 min. This strategy is broadly applicable to a library of 16 COFs spanning β-ketoenamine, hydrazone, imine, and imide linkages, yielding decimeter-scale monoliths with designable structural colors across the visible spectrum. By integrating periodic macroporosity, permanent framework porosity, and photonic functionality into one material platform, the resulting IO COF PhCs enable cross-scale programmable optical encoding and visually self-reporting adsorption. The application potential of IO COF PhCs is demonstrated for biomimetic anti-counterfeiting patterns and structural-color-indicated Au capture. This work establishes a general route toward crystalline IO COF PhCs and provides a versatile platform for coupling molecular functionality with photonic regulation in advanced smart materials.

title: Self‐Assembled Supramolecular Host–Guest Composite Enables Interfacial Regulation Toward Dendrite‐Free Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The instability of zinc anodes during reversible deposition and dissolution in the aqueous electrolyte constitutes a critical bottleneck limiting the lifespan of aqueous zinc‐ion batteries (AZIBs). Herein, we utilize a straightforward and supramolecular self‐assembly approach involving 4‐sulfocalix[6]arene (SCA[6]) and N,N’‐dimethyl‐9,9’‐biacridinium dinitrate (LCG), driven by cooperative host‐guest recognition and electrostatic forces. The spontaneous interfacial assembly of these components enables the construction of a protective interphase on zinc anodes and functions as a “molecular switch” to regulate the Zn 2 + solvation structure, facilitate ion transport, and accommodate volumetric fluctuations during cycling. Consequently, the LCG/SCA[6]‐modified interface effectively mitigates corrosion and dendrite growth, thereby significantly enhancing the electrochemical stability and cycling performance of AZIBs. As a result, the (LCG/SCA[6]) 2 ‐Zn symmetric cell can maintain stable operation for over 3800 h at 1 mA cm −2 and 1 mAh cm −2 . The (LCG/SCA[6]) 2 ‐Zn||I 2 coin cell retains a specific capacity of 200.50 mAh g −1 with a capacity retention rate of 87.25% at 2 A g −1 even after 14 000 cycles. Considering the low cost and simplicity of LCG/SCA[6] film fabrication, this supramolecular composite presents a promising strategy for enhancing the stability of zinc anodes.

title: Rapid Flow Synthesis of Zr‐MOF Nanoparticles in Supercritical CO 2 for Toxic Chemical Removal
abstract: ABSTRACT Zirconium‐based metal‐organic frameworks (Zr‐MOFs) are promising materials for the adsorption and degradation of toxic chemicals; however, their scalable synthesis is hindered by the slow formation of Zr–oxo clusters. Here, we report rapid flow synthesis of Zr‐MOF nanoparticles in supercritical carbon dioxide (scCO 2 ). Using UiO‐66 as a model system, we observe fast particle formation (17 s) and achieve 54% ± 0.28% yield in 75 s with an averaged BET surface area of 1274 ± 38 m 2 g −1 . Possible contributing factors to the fast nucleation include reduced solvent polarity, fast mass transfer, and modulated solute miscibility with the scCO 2 /DMF medium. Acid modulators appear to be critical for regulating Zr‐oxo cluster formation and the morphological transition from nanoparticle aggregates to single crystals. This strategy is extended to the synthesis of high‐quality UiO‐66‐NH 2 and MOF‐808. Products of the rapidly synthesized UiO series were evaluated for chemical warfare agent (CWA) simulant decomposition and TICs adsorption. UiO‐66‐NH 2 showed faster DMNP hydrolysis and higher NH 3 , Cl 2 , and CK uptake than UiO‐66, with performance comparable to MOFs produced by days‐long batch synthesis.

title: Anisotropic Near‐Infrared Amplified Spontaneous Emission in Single‐Benzene Organic Crystals
abstract: ABSTRACT Organic materials capable of near‐infrared (NIR) amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) are attractive for compact photonic and sensing technologies, yet efficient NIR ASE typically requires extended π‐conjugated frameworks. Herein, we report a structurally simple donor– π –acceptor (D– π –A) dye molecule, butyl (2E,4E)‐2‐cyano‐5‐(4‐(dimethylamino)phenyl)penta‐2,4‐dienoate ( M1 ), containing only a single benzene ring, that exhibits efficient NIR emission and ASE. Despite its limited π ‐conjugation, M1 crystals show a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of up to 19% and NIR emission centered at 760 nm with a large Stokes shift. Notably, M1 crystals over a broad range of dimensions exhibit ASE, indicating that ASE generation does not require a narrowly defined crystal size. The ASE response also varies substantially with crystallographic orientation. Block‐ and plate‐like crystals exhibit direction‐dependent ASE along distinct crystallographic axes, whereas rod‐ and needle‐like crystals simultaneously generate two ASE bands centered at approximately 750 and 670 nm along the growth direction. In contrast, the analogous tert‐butyl derivative exhibits markedly weaker emission and no detectable ASE, underscoring the importance of substituent flexibility and crystal packing. These results show that pronounced and direction‐dependent NIR ASE can be realized in organic crystals with remarkably limited π ‐conjugation.

title: A Porous Polymer of Thienothiophene and Tetraphenylethylene: Design, Synthesis and Photophysical Properties
abstract: A novel conjugated porous polymer (CPP) based on thieno[3,2-b]thiophene (TT) and tetraphenylethylene (TPE) was successfully designed and synthesized via a Pd(0)-catalyzed Suzuki cross-coupling reaction. Owing to its rigid, highly cross-linked architecture, the resulting TT–TPE polymer is insoluble and exhibits permanent porosity. Comprehensive characterization using UV–Vis, fluorescence, and FTIR spectroscopy, together with scanning electron microscopy (SEM), cyclic voltammetry (CV), and thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), confirmed the successful formation of a robust π-conjugated porous network. The polymer exhibits a strong π–π* absorption band at 392 nm, intense fluorescence emission at 549 nm, and a large Stokes shift, indicating efficient intramolecular energy transfer and significant excited-state relaxation. SEM images reveal a hierarchically porous, sponge-like morphology, while electrochemical studies demonstrate stable redox behavior and favorable HOMO and LUMO energy levels, highlighting its potential for optoelectronic applications. Furthermore, the optical and electrochemical band gaps are in good agreement, indicating the reliability of the experimental results. Density functional theory (DFT) calculations further corroborate the experimental findings, showing excellent agreement between the simulated and observed electronic transitions. Overall, the TT–TPE conjugated porous polymer represents a promising functional material for applications in chemical sensing, energy storage, and optoelectronic devices.

title: Comparative Analysis of Poly(Ethylene Glycol) (PEG) and Poly(2‐Ethyl‐2‐Oxazoline) (PEtOx) for Organic Solvent‐Free Lipid Nanoparticle Formulations
abstract: ABSTRACT Efficient, biocompatible, and flexible application of CRISPR‐Cas9 remains a major challenge in gene therapy. This study addresses a novel formulation method, focusing on organic solvent‐free lipid nanoparticles for the efficient delivery of CRISPR‐Cas9 components. Therefore, novel stealth lipids comprising the lipid anchor cholesterol hemisuccinate conjugated to poly(2‐ethyl‐2‐oxazoline) (PEtOx) were synthesized and evaluated as a promising in vitro alternative to commercially available poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)‐based lipids. Our study identified PEtOx‐lipids as markedly more biocompatible compared to PEG‐based analogues (12‐fold reduction in cytotoxicity; 99% reduced hemolytic effect) with high efficiency for mRNA gene delivery. We demonstrate successful CRISPR‐Cas9 activity ex vivo and efficient uptake of PEtOx nanoparticles by macrophages in vivo (66.5% pos. F4/80 + macrophages). Our data demonstrate that PEtOx‐based stealth lipids are a promising alternative to PEG. The resulting LNPs, optimized for fully aqueous manufacturing, address key limitations of current LNP systems, including immunogenicity and the reliance on ethanol‐based production processes.

title: Lithium‐Salt‐Driven Lewis Pair Polymerization for Chemically Recyclable and Ion‐Conductive Polyester Elastomers
abstract: ABSTRACT Herein, we report a lithium‐salt‐driven Lewis pair polymerization (LPP) strategy to accomplish controlled polyester synthesis, ionic conductivity, and closed‐loop recyclability within a single platform. The combination of commercial lithium salts (LiTFSI or LiCF 3 SO 3 ) and a novel bifunctional N ‐heterocyclic olefin (NHO) enables rapid and living ring‐opening polymerization of diverse lactones ( ε ‐caprolactone, δ ‐valerolactone, and rac ‐lactide) under mild conditions, affording well‐defined block copolymers with predictable molecular weights and narrow molecular weight distributions. Kinetic and mechanistic studies reveal a nonclassical zero‐order dependence on the concentrations of both monomer and Lewis acid, governed by the multi‐coordination capability of lithium cations. Distinct from traditional polymerizations, the residual lithium salts are retained in situ to impart competitive ionic conductivity, which enables the fabrication of ion‐conductive polyester elastomers with highly tunable mechanical properties ( ε ∼229%‒2111% and σ ∼1.6‒37.4 MPa) and room‐temperature ionic conductivities (up to 10 −5 S/cm) through a one‐step protocol. A comprehensive evaluation of the strain sensitivity, electrical hysteresis, response/recovery behavior, and cyclic sensing performance supports their potential for applications in reliable, real‐time flexible strain sensing. Furthermore, both the polyester matrix and lithium salts can be efficiently recovered, realizing full closed‐loop recycling. This catalyst‐to‐function paradigm provides a general blueprint for integrating catalysis, functionality, and circularity in polymer design.

title: Zinc‐Catalyzed Dehydrogenative Alkynylation of BN‐Polycyclic Aromatics
abstract: ABSTRACT We report a zinc‐catalyzed dehydrogenative alkynylation of BN‐polycyclic aromatics with terminal alkynes, enabling efficient access to BN‐embedded phenylacetylene scaffolds via direct B─H/C─H coupling. This transformation proceeds under mild conditions with broad substrate scope, accommodating diverse BN‐polycyclic aromatics and aryl, heteroaryl, and alkyl alkynes, as well as functionally complex substrates, with excellent functional group tolerance. The method is scalable and enables facile downstream derivatization. Photophysical studies reveal tunable absorption and emission properties governed by π‐extension and BN incorporation, distinct from all‐carbon analogues. Mechanistic studies support a pathway involving alkynyl–zinc intermediates and rate‐determining B─H activation, accompanied by H 2 evolution. This work provides a general and efficient strategy for constructing BN‐containing π‐conjugated systems with potential in functional materials and molecular design.

title: Cisplatin Conjugated with Vinylsulfonamide Cross-Links Pyruvate Kinase M2 to Trigger Ferroptosis
abstract: Abstract Cisplatin serves as a first-line chemotherapeutic agent due to its DNA binding property. However, this intrinsic electrophilicity drives off-target interactions with proteins, which compromises anticancer efficacy, and also suggests the presence of unexplored targets. To identify platinum-binding proteins, a class of platinum(II) complexes containing a covalent vinylsulfonamide group were designed to provide stronger affinity for target engagement. By using competitive chemical proteomics technology, pyruvate kinase M2 (PKM2) was identified as the direct target of Pt1. The intracellular binding involved the recognition of the Cys49 pocket via cis-platinum moiety, which was strengthened by the synergistic event of platinum-centered ligand exchange and vinylsulfonamide-mediated covalent anchoring. This effective multimodal interaction disrupted PKM2 oligomerization and promoted its nuclear translocation. Subsequently, Pt1 induced ferroptosis via the PKM2-HMOX1 axis, further enhanced by mitochondrial oxidative stress. In xenograft models, Pt1 exhibited antitumor efficacy comparable to that of cisplatin, along with lower hepatotoxicity. This study presents a cisplatin conjugate that induces ferroptosis through intramolecular protein cross-linking, providing a synergistic coordination-covalent strategy for nonclassical platinum-based therapeutics.

title: Activation‐Free and Strain‐Resilient Island‐Bridge Liquid Metal Inks for Machine‐Learning‐Enabled Epidermal Electromyography
abstract: ABSTRACT Liquid metal particle‐based inks offer a scalable route toward stretchable electronics, yet their practical implementation is hindered by activation‐dependent conductivity and poor electrical stability under deformation. Herein, we report an intrinsically conductive and strain‐resilient liquid metal ink with a rationally engineered island‐bridge micro‐architecture, in which Cu‐decorated carbon nanotubes (CuCNTs) bridge adjacent liquid metal particles (LMPs) through initial hydrogen‐bonding/coordination‐assisted attachment to the native gallium‐oxide shell, followed by local Cu‐Ga alloying at the CuCNTs/LMPs interface. Enabled by solvent‐mediated dispersion and interfacial hybridization, the strain‐resilient composite ink supports high‐resolution (100 µm) screen printing and deformable circuit integration. The dynamically reconfigurable island‐bridge network retains a sheet resistance of 1.3 × 10 −1 Ω sq −1 at 300% strain, together with stable resistance during prolonged cyclic stretching and bending. When printed into a compact 12‐channel array on breathable fibrous substrates, the resulting electrode array exhibits low skin‐electrode impedance and superior high‐density surface electromyography (HD‐sEMG) performance compared with commercial gel electrodes. Combined with machine‐learning‐assisted analysis, the electromyography arrays enable training‐state recognition, individualized load assessment, and continuous monitoring of fatigue‐associated exercise states during dynamic exercise. This work provides a scalable strategy for intrinsically conductive liquid metal electronics and advances their application in intelligent wearable biointerfaces and soft electronic systems.

title: Intermolecular Interaction Engineering for Efficient Large‐Area Tin‐based Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Poly(3,4‐ethylenedioxythiophene):poly(styrenesulfonate) (PEDOT:PSS) has been widely used as a hole transport layer (HTL) in environmentally friendly tin‐based perovskite solar cells (TPSCs). However, its intrinsic weak acidity and strong tendency toward molecular aggregates hinder its performance in TPSCs. Here, we develop a molecular engineering strategy by introducing a p‐type small molecule, 4,4'‐(5,6‐bis(2‐methoxyethoxy)benzo[c][1,2,5]thiadiazole‐4,7‐diyl)bis(2,5‐difluoro‐N,N‐bis(4‐methoxyphenyl)aniline) (FEG), to modify PEDOT:PSS and, crucially, employ a comprehensive set of solid‐state nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques to directly elucidate the intermolecular interactions governing this modification. Magic‐angle spinning 1 H NMR, 1 H‐ 1 H double‐quantum‐single‐quantum correlation spectroscopy, and variable spinning‐rate measurements reveal strong interactions between FEG and PSS that redistribute the PEDOT:PSS microstructure and promote greater charge delocalization within the conductive polymer network. This interaction improves PEDOT:PSS dispersion, neutralizes residual acidity and enhances interfacial wettability, enabling the growth of high‐quality Sn‐based perovskite films with enlarged grains, reduced defect density and relieved residual stress. As a result, trap‐assisted recombination is suppressed and hole extraction is improved. Consequently, FEG‐PEDOT:PSS‐based TPSCs achieve a record efficiency of 14.92% for 1‐cm 2 devices and a champion efficiency of 17.02% for 0.04‐cm 2 devices, substantially outperforming their pristine PEDOT counterparts. Furthermore, these devices exhibit excellent operational stability, maintaining over 85% of their initial efficiency after 1100 h of storage under a N 2 atmosphere.

title: Hydrogen‐Bond‐Assisted Secondary Amine‐Phosphonate Tandem Sites on Mesoporous Nano‐Silica for Uranyl Carbonate Capture From Alkaline Wastewater
abstract: ABSTRACT The selective capture of uranium from alkaline radioactive wastewater remains highly challenging because uranyl carbonate complexes, particularly [UO 2 (CO 3 ) 3 ] 4− , possess remarkable thermodynamic stability and electrostatic repulsion from negatively charged adsorbent surfaces. Herein, we report a secondary‐sphere activation strategy by constructing secondary amine‐phosphonate tandem sites within mesoporous nano‐silica channels (GP@SiO 2 ‐APTES) for efficient uranyl carbonate capture. The rationally integrated secondary amine groups and phosphonate moieties establish a cooperative binding microenvironment, in which hydrogen‐bond‐donating secondary amine sites facilitate carbonate activation while adjacent phosphonate groups provide strong uranium coordination. As a result, GP@SiO 2 ‐APTES achieves a remarkable adsorption capacity of 348.8 mg g − 1 toward [UO 2 (CO 3 ) 3 ] 4− under alkaline conditions (pH 8–10), significantly outperforming monofunctional control materials. Combined spectroscopic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal that the secondary amine‐assisted secondary coordination environment weakens uranyl‐carbonate interactions and promotes phosphonate‐mediated uranium binding. Moreover, the hybrid silica framework exhibits excellent operational durability, retaining over 99% uranium removal efficiency after 250 kGy γ‐irradiation and five adsorption–desorption cycles. This work demonstrates a molecular design strategy that employs hydrogen‐bond‐assisted secondary coordination to facilitate the capture of stable metal complexes, providing new opportunities for advanced actinide separation materials.

title: Fluorophore-Conjugated Diphenylalanine Peptides Reveal Self-Sorting in a Multicomponent Supramolecular System
abstract: The interplay between distinct molecular building blocks in multicomponent supramolecular systems can lead to co-assembly or self-sorting, yet distinguishing between these modes of organization remains challenging. Here, we developed two intrinsically fluorescent derivatives of the self-assembling dipeptide diphenylalanine (FF): nitrobenzoxadiazole-conjugated FF (NBD-FF) and a coumarin-conjugated tert-butyloxycarbonyl-protected FF derivative (BocFF-DAC). Both derivatives formed fibrillar assemblies while exhibiting spectrally distinct fluorescence, enabling their direct visualization by confocal microscopy. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction of NBD-FF revealed an extended hydrogen-bonded lattice in which the NBD moiety participates directly in intermolecular interactions, including aromatic, hydrophobic, and hydrogen-bonding contacts. This finding demonstrates that the fluorophore acts as an active structural element rather than a passive label. When NBD-FF and BocFF-DAC were assembled together, confocal microscopy revealed predominantly spatially distinct fibrillar populations with limited overlap, consistent with preferential self-sorting rather than uniform co-assembly. These findings establish fluorophore-conjugated short peptides as intrinsically traceable building blocks for investigating multicomponent supramolecular organization, while highlighting that fluorophore conjugation can simultaneously enable visualization and influence the assembly.

title: Electrochemical Synthesis of Silver Icosahedrons for SERS Sensing Applications
abstract: ABSTRACT Ag icosahedrons, characterized by the size‐dependent distribution of strain fields, has garnered increasing interests across disciplines from crystallography to materials science. However, the metastability arising from such intrinsic strain greatly restricts the available synthetic routes. Here, we present a facile aqueous‐phase electrodeposition technique for the robust synthesis of Ag icosahedrons. By decreasing the Ag reduction rate, we achieve enhanced control over the electrodeposition kinetics, as quantitatively evidenced by the apparent activation energy. The pronounced kinetic stability allows for the synthesis of particles up to 5 µm in size within 10 min (Pretreatment time: 48 h). Through systematic variation of applied potentials, currents, and electrolyte compositions, we enable the design of Ag icosahedrons with tunable hierarchical structures. These structured particles can be effectively employed as surface‐enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS) substrates for pesticide detection. This work establishes a stable and pure model system that facilitates the straightforward synthesis of metastable structures.

title: Tuning Coordination Chemistry and Composition of Metal–Organic Frameworks for Efficient Hydrogen Production
abstract: ABSTRACT Improving the cost and efficiency of hydrogen production via water splitting is a long‐standing research challenge in support of carbon neutrality goals. Optimising the structural composition and coordination chemistry of metal−organic frameworks (MOFs) can yield suitable catalysts or supports that enhance hydrogen production efficiency. MOFs offer precise control over porosity, metal nodes and linker chemistry that is unattainable with conventional catalysts. This review provides a critical, cross‐cutting assessment of MOF‐based catalysis across electrochemical (EC) and photo(electro)chemical (PC and PEC) water‐splitting technologies. We systematically analyse how key structural features (ultrahigh porosity, surface area and compositional changes) and coordination chemistry (tunable metal active sites and functionalised linkers) govern catalytic activity and stability. For electrochemical systems, we critically examine the multifunctionality of pristine MOFs, their conductive carbon‐based derivatives and the synergistic performance of MOF/carbon and MOF/metal hybrids. For MOF‐driven PC and PEC water splitting, we examine MOF selectivity and the mechanisms of light absorption, charge separation and interfacial electron transfer that enable MOFs to serve as integrated platforms bridging light harvesting and redox catalysis. Notably, we devote dedicated sections to limitations in charge‐carrier dynamics and defect engineering, significant bottlenecks that are often overlooked yet key to future performance breakthroughs. A machine‐learning perspective is briefly included, with case studies presented as an emerging design tool for predicting hydrogen adsorption capacity and optimising hydrogen production activity via MOF‐based catalysts. Finally, the review concludes with targeted future directions aimed at accelerating the transition from laboratory discovery to practical, sustainable hydrogen production.

title: Early-life bovine respiratory virome analysis reveals phage-driven adaptation and cross-host evolutionary signatures
abstract: Abstract Past outbreaks of zoonotic viral infections highlight the importance of understanding respiratory virome ecology. As major food-producing animals with frequent human contact, cattle represent a critical host at the human-animal interface; however, the early-life establishment of their respiratory virome and its evolutionary connections to viruses from other hosts remain underexplored. Here, we longitudinally profile the upper respiratory tract (URT) virome of beef calves from birth to weaning using an optimized viral enrichment procedure and metagenomic workflow. Viral communities exhibited increased richness and turnover, reflecting ecological structuring during early life. Temperate phages dominate the URT phage community and share virulence- and mobility-associated genes with bacterial hosts, likely contributing to host adaptation and colonization persistence. Vertebrate-associated viruses emerge after the first week of life. Targeted reassembly from bovine URT viromes recovers near-complete betacoronavirus-like (CoV-D180) and adenovirus-like (AdV-D56) genomes positioned phylogenetically between bovine and human viral lineages. Competitive mapping of bovine-derived CoV-D180 and AdV-D56 to human respiratory metatranscriptomic datasets reveals genome-specific, regionally structured coverage patterns distinct from reference viruses, supporting shared sequence features in conserved genomic regions across host-associated viral lineages. Collectively, these findings reveal early-life assembly dynamics of the bovine respiratory virome and highlight cross-host signatures in a One Health framework.

title: Photoinduced Electron Transfer in a Two-Dimensional Conductive Metal–Organic Framework
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional metal–organic frameworks offer a rare combination of porosity and conductivity. However, designing ligands that imbue frameworks with efficient charge transport pathways but also permit further functionalization of the ligand structure is not trivial. Towards this end, we leverage the amphoteric and ambipolar nature of phenanthroimidazole moieties to design ligands in which ionic and electronic states are intertwined. This approach forms the basis for a materials platform that is responsive and provides a mechanism for conductance contrast. We detail the synthesis of a new ligand, H8(BPI-P), and describe its optical and electronic properties. We show that these properties are retained upon incorporation into a 2D framework, Cu2(BPI-P), leading to higher-than-expected electrical conductivity that can be externally modulated. The ligand—a near-perfect rhombus—also enables Lozenge tiling in two dimensions, further identifying symmetry as an emerging means of tuning the properties of 2D framework materials.

title: NiFe Metal–Organic Framework Film Infiltrated With Conjugated Molecules: An Efficient and Durable Anode for Alkaline Seawater Oxidation at Ampere‐Level Current Density
abstract: Although holding great promise to mitigate freshwater scarcity for green hydrogen production, direct seawater electrolysis is challenged by the anodic chloride oxidation reactions, which lowers the system efficiency and cause catalyst corrosion. Herein, we demonstrate a strategy for realizing efficient and long‐lasting alkaline seawater oxidation over a NiFe metal–organic framework (NiFe MOF) film supported on Ni foam via infiltratation with the conjugated molecule 7,7,8,8‐tetracyanoquinododimethane (TCNQ). Such TCNQ@NiFe MOF/NF anode is capable of attaining an industrial‐level current density of 1000 mA cm −2 with a low overpotential of 352 mV and maintaining 800‐h operational stability. The incorporated TCNQ molecules can enhance the electronic conductivity, effectively repel Cl − , and suppress Fe leaching. An anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer built from TCNQ@NiFe MOF/NF and Pt/C/NF operates stably for 450 h.

title: Homogenizing Fullerene Contacts by Supramolecular Host–Guest Assembly for Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Fullerene and its derivatives are widely adopted as electron transport layers (ETLs) in high‐performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, fullerene materials are prone to aggregation and rearrangement under environmental stress, which acts as one of the critical factors restricting the long‐term operational stability of devices. Here, we report a host–guest supramolecular assembly strategy using rigid triptycene (TPC) molecules to stabilize fullerene‐based ETLs. The [6,6]‐phenyl‐C 61 ‐butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM)–TPC host–guest interaction enables the spatial isolation and noncovalent immobilization of PCBM cages, which suppresses the thermal‐driven aggregation, crystallization, and morphological variation of PCBM layers. The resulting inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.83%, with 96.0% efficiency retention after 1000 h of 85°C thermal aging and 92.3% retention after 1000 h of 85°C photothermal maximum power point tracking. This work offers a supramolecular solution for high‐stability optoelectronic devices.

title: Hydrodynamic Selection of Polymorphic Assembly Pathways in Plant Protein Amyloid Fibrils
abstract: Plant protein amyloid fibrils are universally assembled in liquid environments, yet their formation is often analyzed without explicitly considering the role of fluid motion. In practice, as a typical model system, soy protein amyloid fibrils (SAFs) are generated under dynamic hydrodynamic conditions involving shear and vortex transport. How such flow fields regulate fibril growth pathways and give rise to polymorphic assembly remains largely unexplored. Here, we elucidate the hydrodynamic selection of SAFs assembly pathways through nanoscale structural characterization combined with flow-field analysis. Atomic force microscopy (AFM) identifies six distinct fibril morphologies, including short-curved, javelin-like, loop-like, twisted ribbon, helical ribbon, and rod-like structures. By integrating AFM observations with particle image velocimetry (PIV) results, we propose a drafting, kissing, and docking (DKD) dynamic as a plausible hydrodynamic model for understanding polymorphic fibril assembly. Computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations further reproduce key characteristics of the experimentally observed flow fields and provide hydrodynamic support for the proposed interpretation of fibrillation pathways. These results demonstrate that an in-depth understanding of hydrodynamic selection behavior in polymorphic assembly pathways is important to pave the way for production of tailormade amyloid materials.
